headline: I Sold My Family’s Traditional Gold Crockery To 'Buy The Dip' And Now I Eat Daal From A Paper Plane
body:
When the Sensex dropped 777 points on Sunday, my WhatsApp investment group, 'Bulls of Bharat,' told me it was a golden opportunity to average out. I didn't want to miss the bus, so I quietly took my grandmother’s heirloom brass thali set to the local jeweler. I figured if the Nifty was below 23,118, the universe was practically begging me to become a Warren Buffett-style tycoon by Monday morning.

I poured every rupee I got from the scrap metal into an obscure mid-cap stock that promised 'Fed-proof stability.' By the time the markets opened, my brokerage app had more red on it than a wedding saree showroom during peak season. My portfolio wasn't just in the red; it was undergoing a existential crisis, shedding value faster than a local train sheds passengers at a suburban station.

Now, my kitchen is basically a minimalist art installation. I’ve traded silver spoons for folded sheets of A4 paper, and my dinner consists of whatever I can scoop up using a cardboard origami crane. My grandmother keeps asking where her serving bowls are, and I just tell her they’re 'highly liquid assets' currently undergoing a strategic, long-term migration. I’m confident that once the Fed stops scaring the markets, I’ll be back to using real metal, but for now, I’m just trying to keep my dinner from folding under the pressure.
caption: Selling the family silver to time the market is a classic move. Just make sure you don't run out of origami paper before the next Fed meeting. #Sensex #StockMarketIndia #FinancialAdvisor #InvestSmartly (satire)
